newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq shows Uday driving car in Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Iraq shows Uday driving car in Baghdad.

text.p: Iraqi television showed Uday, eldest son of President Saddam Hussein, driving his car along the street where he was shot and seriously wounded almost five months ago.

Uday was seen on television late on Wednesday sitting behind the wheel of his red Porsche convertible beside another man, probably a bodyguard. Babel newspaper said on Thursday Uday had visited the area where he was shot on December 12.
Uday was also shown receiving wellwishers as he sat in an arm chair wearing black shoes and moving both hands -- the first time he had been shown out of bed or a wheelchair.

Since the shooting Uday underwent several operations, the last on April 12 on his left leg. Foreign doctors were said to have helped treat Uday, who is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, owns Babel and runs the Shabab television channel.
Uday, who said he was hit in both legs, said after the operation he expected to be on his feet in a few days or weeks. His Iraqi doctor said he believed it was the last operation needed.
A few days after the assassination attempt, Uday blamed Iran. Tehran denied the charge.
